title: "Horizon Europe topics"
format:
  html:
    toc: true

---

The Horizon Europe topic index is an OpenSearch index of the topics (calls for proposals) of the current Horizon
Europe work programme, built from the official work programme PDFs. Two features of
[crisalid-agents](https://github.com/CRISalid-esr/crisalid-agents) rely on it:

- the **Horizon topic finder** (`project_topic_matching` agent): a chat agent that finds the topics matching a project
  idea, served by OpenWebUI and by the chat API;
- the **Topic-to-Researcher Match** (TRM): a batch that matches every topic of a cluster with the researchers of the
  laboratories, from their publications in the knowledge graph, and produces evaluation reports.

## Services and configuration

| Profile | Service | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `horizon_europe_index` | `opensearch` | Single-node OpenSearch holding the topic index (port 9200, internal) |
| `crisalid-agents-batch` | `crisalid-agents-batch` | One-shot container for the index ingestion and the TRM batch, run on demand with `docker compose run` (never by `up`) |

Both are included in the main Docker Compose stack (see [Docker Compose](docker-compose.qmd)). The OpenSearch
instance (`docker/horizon-europe-index/`) is only reachable on the internal agents network, over plain HTTP and without
authentication: the security plugin is disabled. Its data lives in the `horizon_opensearch_data` named volume.

Configuration files:

- `docker/horizon-europe-index/.env` (copy of `.env.sample`): only the heap size, `OPENSEARCH_HEAP=1g`. The file must
  exist even if the profile is never started, because the main compose file includes it.
- `docker/crisalid-agents/.env`: the index settings (`HORIZON_OS_URL`, `HORIZON_OS_INDEX`, `HORIZON_SEARCH_PIPELINE`,
  defaults are fine), the agents served (`CRISALID_AGENTS_AGENTS`, which includes `project_topic_matching` by default)
  and `TRM_MODEL` (the model of the TRM batch, empty to reuse the chat model).
- `docker/.env`: the shared `EMBEDDING_*` variables. The ingestion and the searches embed texts through this endpoint,
  so it must be configured first (see [Semantic Embeddings](embeddings.qmd)).

The `crisalid-agents-batch` service is built from the chat API image, the only one shipping the batch scripts, and
mounts two host directories of `docker/horizon-europe-index/`: `wp/` (the PDFs, read-only, mounted as
`/data/horizon`) and `reports/` (the TRM reports). Both are ignored by git.

## 1. Upload the work programme PDFs

Download the work programme parts of the current programme from the
[Funding & Tenders portal](https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/programmes/horizon)
(reference documents of Horizon Europe: one PDF per cluster, e.g. `wp-5-culture-creativity-and-inclusive-society_horizon-2026-2027_en.pdf`),
and copy them into `docker/horizon-europe-index/wp/` on the server. For instance with sftp, as the user owning the
deployment:

```bash
sftp crisalid@<server>
sftp> cd /opt/crisalid/crisalid-deployment/docker/horizon-europe-index/wp
sftp> put *.pdf
sftp> bye
```

Only the cluster parts are useful (the agent and the batch work per cluster, CL1 to CL6); other parts of the programme
are ignored or produce parse warnings.

## 2. Build the index

From `docker/`, as the user owning the deployment. `docker compose run` starts the OpenSearch service if needed and
waits for it to be healthy before running the command.

Pull the images first, then check the PDFs parse correctly without touching the index (`--issues` prints every parse
warning):

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.dev.yaml pull opensearch crisalid-agents-batch

docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.dev.yaml \
  run --rm crisalid-agents-batch python scripts/index_horizon_topics.py --dry-run --issues
```

Then build the index. The first run (or a rebuild after a change of the embedding model) uses `--recreate`, which drops
and recreates the index and its search pipelines:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.dev.yaml \
  run --rm crisalid-agents-batch python scripts/index_horizon_topics.py --recreate
```

Every topic and passage is embedded through the embedding endpoint, so the run takes a few minutes. It ends with a
summary of the files and topics indexed, and `complete=True, ok=True` when everything went through. `--report
<file>` writes the same summary as JSON.

### Updating the programme

Add, replace or remove PDFs in `wp/` and run the ingestion again, without `--recreate`:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.dev.yaml \
  run --rm crisalid-agents-batch python scripts/index_horizon_topics.py
```

The ingestion is idempotent: unchanged files (same content, parser and embedding model) are skipped, and after a
complete run the topics of files that are no longer in the directory are removed from the index.

## 3. Serve the Horizon topic finder

Once the index is built, start (or restart) the agent services together with the index profile, so that they reach
the OpenSearch service:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.dev.yaml \
  --profile horizon_europe_index --profile neo4j-mcp \
  --profile crisalid-agents-owui --profile crisalid-agents-chat-api \
  up -d
```

Both agent services serve the graph agent and the topic finder by default (`CRISALID_AGENTS_AGENTS` in
`docker/crisalid-agents/.env`); chat API clients select the agent they call. In OpenWebUI the topic finder appears as a
model next to the graph agent (see [Configuring OpenWebUI](configuring-openwebui.qmd)).

## 4. Topic-to-Researcher Match

The TRM batch runs in the same `crisalid-agents-batch` service, by hand, and needs the `neo4j-mcp` profile to be up
(it reads the publications through the MCP toolbox). Set `TRM_MODEL` in `docker/crisalid-agents/.env` to use a
dedicated model. The JSON, Markdown and PDF reports are written to `docker/horizon-europe-index/reports/` on the host.

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.dev.yaml --profile neo4j-mcp up -d

docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.dev.yaml \
  run --rm crisalid-agents-batch python scripts/topic_researcher_match.py --list-clusters

docker compose -f docker-compose.yaml -f docker-compose.dev.yaml \
  run --rm crisalid-agents-batch python scripts/topic_researcher_match.py --cluster CL2
```

A single topic can be rerun with `--topic <topic id>`; a failed topic is recorded in the JSON report and never aborts
the cluster.
